transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-05-27 | Start: 14:00 PDT | Duration: ~60m | Attendees: Samira Chen (Redwood AE), Evan Ortiz (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Redwood Product); Michael Lee (AuroraCloud Head of Partnerships), Priya Narayanan (AuroraCloud Solutions Architect), Devon Carter (AuroraCloud Marketplace PM), Rhea Singh (AuroraCloud Security)

[00:00] Samira (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into the marketplace checklist and the reference arch. Evan, you wanna kick with a quick run of what we typically need?

[00:15] Evan (Redwood SE): Sure. Hi all. So typical flow for a Redwood marketplace listing is: we validate the integration surface, confirm auth (SSO/SAML or token), determine deployment mode (hosted listing vs private VPC listing), confirm billing/SKU and pricing, and run an E2E deploy in staging. Important bits for AuroraCloud: do you want a managed hosted experience or a private "Aurora only" listing that uses VPC peering?

[00:40] Michael (AuroraCloud): We want the private listing option ideally. Our enterprise customers ask for single-tenant variants and VPC peering. But we also want a hosted listing for smaller customers. So need both options documented.

[00:55] Priya (AuroraCloud): Just to add, for private we require KMS integration and audit logs forwarded into our SIEM. Also SSO via SAML is required for admin flows.

[01:10] Evan: Yeah, that's totally doable. On KMS, Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM; we need to confirm key rotation processes and whether Aurora wants envelope encryption or direct KMS calls. I realized in our docs sometimes "KV cache" gets transcribed as "KV cash" so just flagging that might confuse the legal folks.

[01:30] Rhea (Security): We also need SOC2 attestation and retention policies spelled out. How long do logs live in Redwood by default?

[01:40] Lina (Product): Default is 30 days for detailed logs in the console; longer retention is an enterprise add-on. We'll include options in the listing template.

[01:50] Michael: Good. On the marketplace listing itself, what's the minimum artifact set? A product description, screenshots, reference arch diagram, security docs, pricing SKU, and a deployment runbook?

[02:05] Samira: Right. We'll send our marketplace listing template that lists required assets. For reference arch we prefer a diagram showing network flows: customer VPC <-> Redwood private connector <-> Redwood Dedicated pool or Hosted, and where KMS and audit logs sit.

[02:25] Priya: Can you show an example?

[02:30] Evan: Sure, I have a sample from a previous partner. (screen share) So here's the minimal ref arch: ingress from Aurora customer, VPC peering to our private connector, optional dedicated GPU pool, KV cache indicated between comp nodes, and KMS calls bubbled out to customer KMS. Note: in older diagrams we labeled it "KV cache" as a component; sometimes customers misread that as storage.

[03:05] Devon (Marketplace PM): On the billing side, we need to agree whether Aurora will bill for the Redwood consumption or if Redwood invoices the end customer and Aurora gets a reseller cut. Typical patterns we've seen?

[03:20] Samira: We support both. For marketplace listings most partners want Redwood to bill and pass-through revenue share. But Aurora could also handle billing if you prefer. We'll need billing contact and contract routing info.

[03:35] Devon: I'll confirm internal billing owner and share the contact.

[03:40] Priya: A technical question: latency SLAs. For private deployments with dedicated pools, what's realistic 95th percentile latency for typical chat workloads?

[03:50] Evan: For short context chat workloads, P95 with dedicated GPU pools and optimized batching is typically 150-350ms per token depending on model and sequence length. We'll provide model-specific perf profiles in the performance appendix. There is a tradeoff between batching (cost) and latency.

[04:10] Michael: That's fine. We'll include expected QPS in the infra doc. Priya will send target QPS.

[04:20] Priya: Yep, I'll send QPS by the end of the week. Also re: SSO, we use SAML with IDP-initiated flows; does Redwood support IDP-initiated?

[04:30] Evan: Yes, SAML SSO with both IDP/ SP-initiated flows is supported; we also have SCIM for user provisioning. We'll include a quick guide in the listing.

[04:45] Rhea: About logs — can we stream audit logs to our SIEM via syslog/HTTP?

[04:50] Lina: We support log forwarding via customer-managed forwarders and delivery to S3/HTTP endpoints. We'll note retention and encryption in transit.

[05:00] Devon: Are there any partner co-marketing assets required? Screens, short blurb, logos?

[05:05] Samira: Yes, logos (SVG), a short 100-200 word blurb, and one or two customer success blurbs if you have them. That helps with marketplace discoverability.

[05:15] Michael: We'll put that together.

[05:20] Evan: One technical nit — for private deployments some customers request on-prem packaging or air-gapped. Redwood has a private deployment package but full on-prem air-gap requires additional security review and a longer timeline. We should flag that as special.

[05:35] Priya: Got it. We're not planning air-gap for the initial launch.

[05:40] Samira: On timelines — typical partner listing goes from agreement to staged listing in 3-6 weeks if everything is ready. Given Aurora wants both hosted and private options, maybe plan for 6-8 weeks to complete both.

[06:00] Devon: Works for us; internal approvals may add a week.

[06:05] Evan: I'll outline a runbook: 1) infra diagram and QPS (Aurora) 2) Redwood shares listing template + security checklist (Redwood) 3) Redwood runs staging deploy and shares logs (Redwood) 4) Aurora validates SSO/KMS and signs off (Aurora) 5) Listing goes live (both). I'll put dates inline after we get the infra diagram.

[06:30] Priya: A quick question on KMS: do you do envelope encryption by default or do partners call the KMS directly? For compliance, we prefer that customer KMS keys never leave our control.

[06:45] Evan: Redwood supports both patterns. Envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS is most common: the application uses a DEK encrypted by the CMK. We'll document the flow and key usage.

[07:05] Rhea: For SOC2 paperwork, can we get a copy of your latest report and your pen test summary?

[07:10] Samira: Yes, I'll share our SOC2 attestation and redacted pen test summary as part of the security pack. We'll need an NDA for full pen test details if required.

[07:25] Michael: Ok. Any blockers on Redwood side we should be aware of?

[07:30] Evan: Nothing major. We'll need the infra diagram and QPS to size a dedicated pool for staging. Also, confirm whether Aurora wants usage-based pricing exposed in the marketplace listing or require pricing off-platform.

[07:45] Devon: We prefer usage-based pricing listed; we'll confirm exact SKUs and minimums.

[07:50] Samira: Great. I'll share the template after this call. We'll also include our recommended quantization and model profiles per workload to help customers pick the right SKU.

[08:05] Priya: One more operational: rollback and fallback. If a model rollout regresses quality, can Redwood automatically fallback to previous model variant?

[08:15] Evan: Yes, we support automatic fallback policies and can do canary rollouts. We'll include a note in the runbook about test prompts and quality monitoring hooks.

[08:30] Samira: Alright let's recap next steps. Priya to share infra diagram + QPS by 2026-06-03. Evan will run staging deploy and share logs by 2026-06-01. Samira to share listing template, security pack (SOC2), and marketplace checklist by 2026-05-29. Devon to confirm billing contact by 2026-05-31. Follow-up sync targeted for 2026-06-10 to review staging listing.

[08:55] Michael: Sounds good. Thank you everyone.

[09:00] Samira: Thanks all, we'll send notes and action items.

End of transcript.
